note: Authored operating rows for direct-response AI UGC performance creative: transformation briefs, public-ad research coding, hook shapes, five-beat scripts, storyboard QA, controlled variants, claim gates, and handoff templates. These rows paraphrase useful mechanisms from the user-supplied article beginning 'Which means anyone can run ads now' but omit its competitor counts, impression claims, costs, accuracy comparisons, research volume, generation volume, and model-quality claims. They are starting hypotheses, not measured results. The full procedure lives in the shared skill ai-ugc-production-pipeline and its performance-creative reference. Hard rules: distinguish observed ad-library facts from performance inference, keep expression original, use only approved proof, review vulnerable-category claims, verify the exact model/runtime before applying syntax, approve the storyboard before paid generation, change one variable per variant, and require approval before spend, upload, publication, or private-asset transfer. Slots are UPPERCASE so an unfilled template trips the deliverable acceptance gate.
omitted: Current ad-platform delivery fields, spend/impression data, model availability, duration/reference/audio/editing limits, provider prices, universal script pace, fixed research sample sizes, and universal performance thresholds are intentionally absent because they are volatile, account-specific, or unverified. Resolve them from current primary evidence, the selected runtime, and owned analytics.

transformationFields.question: who experiences the moment, and which lawful, respectful context makes it recognizable
what observable moment can the first frame or problem beat show without diagnosing or degrading the viewer
what practical or emotional cost follows from the current workflow or misunderstanding
what plausible transformation can the product support without promising an unverified outcome
what exact product action produces value and can be demonstrated honestly
which owned demonstration, scoped metric, licensed testimonial, or sourced comparison may appear
what single next action and downstream event determine whether the creative created business value

active or inactive status exactly as exposed; do not translate active into profitable

the first spoken idea, paraphrased in public deliverables
what communicates before dialogue or captions are understood
the person or situation the opener appears to select
the current belief, blamed cause, and proposed alternative cause
what the product visibly does and how specifically the script explains it
need, trust, effort, urgency, price, desire, or another doubt addressed
demonstration, scoped data, licensed testimonial, comparison, authority, or none
qualification language and the requested next action
confessional, challenge, demo, transformation, interview, news-like, silent visual, or another reusable structure
observed fact versus inference plus footage, likeness, music, trademark, testimonial, and claim concerns

hookShapes.skeleton: [AUDIENCE], this is for the moment when [PAINFUL MOMENT].
hookShapes.guardrail: use only when the label is lawful, respectful, relevant, and not a proxy for discrimination

hookShapes.skeleton: Do you [RECOGNIZABLE ACTION] and still get [UNWANTED RESULT]?
hookShapes.guardrail: the premise must be common enough to recognize and specific enough to answer honestly

hookShapes.skeleton: If [PAINFUL MOMENT], the first thing to check is [REFRAME].
hookShapes.guardrail: present a testable reframe, not a diagnosis or universal causal claim
the result and mechanism require approved proof; do not rely on shock alone

scriptBeats.job: select the intended viewer and stop the scroll
scriptBeats.required: one line, one performance choice, and one first-frame action that point at the same idea

scriptBeats.job: make the painful moment and current-state cost concrete
scriptBeats.required: an observable situation without humiliation, diagnosis, or fabricated causality

scriptBeats.job: show or state the product implementation
scriptBeats.required: a concrete action and result; prepared UI or post-production when text accuracy matters
approved evidence with scope, or an explicit proof gap instead of invention
one lawful next action without false urgency or disguised navigation

storyboardChecks.pass: the target viewer can infer the topic before dialogue begins
the synthetic or consented character fits the audience without copying a real creator
camera, light, room, skin, wardrobe, and performance fit the chosen phone-native or deliberate production style
each beat has one primary state change that can finish inside its timing budget
every visible hand and prop has one clear, physically plausible role
spoken-to-camera and insert or voiceover beats are named and cannot be confused
every beat ends with a visible state the next beat can inherit
identity, wardrobe, voice, time, geography, prop counts, and ownership remain coherent
labels, arrows, frame numbers, logos, timing strips, and annotations are explicitly excluded from final footage
UI, packaging text, subtitles, formulas, and numeric displays move to controlled references or post-production when exactness matters

variantDimensions.holdConstant: speaker, setting, body, demo, proof, CTA, and production treatment
spoken hook, speaker, setting, remaining beats, proof, and CTA
script, setting function, shots, proof, CTA, and edit
speaker, script, beat functions, proof, CTA, and camera role
hook, problem, demo, speaker, setting, and CTA
hook, problem, demo, speaker, setting, and CTA; proof remains approved
hook, problem, demo, proof, speaker, setting, and edit

claimGates.gate: label activity, dates, and visible variants as observed; label winner, spend, conversion, and profit as unknown without owned evidence
reuse the structural lesson while making script, footage, casting, voice, brand devices, and proof original or licensed
remove humiliation and diagnosis; require approved mechanism, scoped evidence, disclosures, and category review
identify the measurement method, source, scope, and approval; otherwise omit the number
verify footage and likeness rights, do not fabricate coverage or endorsement, and label dramatization when required
use original or consented references, preserve disclosure obligations, and never impersonate a real person
verify the exact account, region, runtime, version, live schema, and limits before promising duration, references, audio, editing, resolution, or continuity
